title: review: P10/P11/P22 tool disclosure, shadow: measure tool-definition tokens per role, compute a task-class-based minimal tool set from a Level-0 catalog, log tool_disclosure decisions; allowlists unchanged
spec:
Facts (Planner grep, provenance repo): worker tool exposure is the per-role Claude Code allowlist in spawn.py:24-31 (scout/triage/review/challenge/spec_review/execute; execute is the Claude fallback only, Codex executors get the Codex CLI's own tools); the bus MCP exposes bus_post_result/bus_read/... to workers (orchestrator/bus_mcp.py) and the orchestrator MCP exposes 11 Planner tools (orchestrator/mcp.py:76-170). Tool schemas for Claude Code built-ins are not controlled by this repo, so P10 here means: know what each role is offered, estimate its schema cost, and compute (shadow) the minimum set a task class needs.
Do:
1. orchestrator/tool_catalog.py (new): CATALOG = Level-0 entries {tool_id: {"line": one-line purpose, "category": one of read, search, edit, shell, test, git, bus, memory, graph, browser, executor, review, "est_schema_tokens": int}} for every id that appears in spawn.py allowlists (Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, each Bash(...) pattern as its own id, mcp__bus__* tools) plus the orchestrator MCP tools (codex, codex_reply, spawn_scout, spawn_review, spawn_challenge, spawn_spec_review, merge, status, executor_fallback, hold_account, resume_account). est_schema_tokens: measure MCP tools from their docstring + signature (chars//4) at import time; built-ins use a fixed table with a comment saying they are estimates (Read 350, Grep 400, Glob 200, Edit 300, Write 200, Bash 500 per pattern group, MCP tools measured). `level0(ids) -> str` renders the compact catalog ("- codex — implement software tasks"). `disclosed(role) -> list[str]` parses the allowlist for a role. `tokens(ids) -> int`.
2. `minimal_set(task, role) -> dict` deterministic: categories needed by task_class × role (table in the module: e.g. review → read, search, git, bus; scout → read, search, git, bus; execute refactor → read, search, edit, test, git, bus; execute with tests in acceptance adds test; docs-only scope (all paths .md) drops test and shell). Returns {"keep": ids, "drop": ids, "reason": str, "mandatory": ids} where mandatory = bus_post_result for every role and everything the role's safety needs (never dropped: Read for all, Bash(git *) for review/scout, tests-green for execute).
3. Shadow wiring: in spawn.run_worker (and the Claude execute fallback) when promotion.mode("tool_disclosure") in ("shadow","active") (active treated as shadow with a one-time notify warning): compute disclosed(role), tokens, minimal_set; record decision_log.record(kind="tool_disclosure", subject=task id, candidates=disclosed ids, hard_constraints=mandatory, deterministic={"task_class", "role", "kept", "dropped", "tokens_disclosed", "tokens_minimal"}, selected="allowlist unchanged (shadow)", reason=minimal_set reason, mode=mode); add tool_tokens_disclosed and tool_tokens_minimal to the task's packet_meta so bus.log_run carries them into the run's context (bus.py copied keys). The allowlist passed to the worker is byte-identical to today (assert in a test).
4. P22 measurement hooks: `tool_catalog.recovery_events(root)` scans runs for rows where a worker asked for a tool outside its allowlist (grep the existing run rows for permission denials if any field carries them; if none exists today, document that this signal is not yet recorded and return an empty list with a note field). context_scorecard gains per-role columns tool_tokens_disclosed (avg) and tool_tokens_minimal (avg) and tool_reduction = minimal/disclosed.
5. Codex executors: record the same tool_disclosure decision with role "codex_execute" using a fixed CODEX_TOOLS entry ("codex CLI built-ins; not controlled here", est 0) so the scorecard shows the gap honestly.
Tests (unittest, `import _harness` first): tests/test_tool_catalog.py::test_catalog_covers_every_allowlisted_id (every id parsed from spawn allowlists has a CATALOG entry), ::test_minimal_set_never_drops_mandatory, ::test_docs_only_task_drops_test_and_shell; tests/test_spawn.py::test_worker_allowlist_unchanged_under_tool_disclosure_shadow (the allowed-tools argument built for a review worker is identical with mode off and shadow; a tool_disclosure decision row exists in shadow only). docs/context-economy/06-tool-disclosure.md (≤60 lines): the catalog, the category table, what shadow logs, what active would do (P11 escalation path: a worker that needs a hidden optional tool posts a bus event and the Planner re-spawns with the wider set; not implemented), revert path (mode off).
Do not change any allowlist string. Do not ask questions; decide and note decisions in the result.
acceptance: docs/context-economy/06-tool-disclosure.md exists; spawn.py allowlist strings unchanged (git diff shows no change to lines 24-31 values); .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0

comments.issue: The `needed` category set for role "execute" never includes "shell", and no other code path adds it. So Bash(npm *), Bash(npx *), Bash(uv *), Bash(python3 *), Bash(bash skills/*) land in `drop` for every execute task unconditionally, not only for docs-only scope as the diff/docs claim ("A docs-only scope drops optional test and shell tools"). Verified: minimal_set({'task_class':'feature','scope':['x.py'],'acceptance':['implement feature']}, 'execute') drops all five shell tools exactly like a docs-only task does. This makes tests/test_tool_catalog.py::test_docs_only_task_drops_test_and_shell pass without actually proving docs-only-specific behavior for shell (it would pass for any execute task), and it systematically overstates the 'minimal' token count / reduction ratio the whole P22 measurement exists to report honestly, for any execute task that legitimately needs npm/python3/uv/bash-skills.

`_task_class` duplicates the codebase's canonical `attribution.task_class` (orchestrator/attribution.py:128) but with an incompatible vocabulary: attribution infers security/architectural/debugging/mechanical/unfamiliar, while this helper checks task.get('task_class') or constraints.get('task_class') and otherwise hardcodes 'refactor'. No production code sets constraints.task_class to 'refactor'/'feature'/'fix'/'test'/'docs' (grep confirms), so the task_class-gated branch in minimal_set (line ~117, 'if role==execute and task_class not in {...}: needed.discard(test)') is effectively dead in production and always falls through to the default. Low impact today since the docs-only path and mandatory tests-green override compensate, but it's a second, silent source of inaccurate 'minimal' measurements and diverges from the module's own reason string which cites task_class as if it were meaningful.
